$comment: What this repository contributes to a running stack, and what a check may
believe about it. `checked` is proved against this repository by
crates/gateway/tests/manifest.rs in this repository's own CI; `declared` is a
statement nobody can verify and carries its own `why`.
THIS IS THE ONE THE WHOLE MECHANISM WAS BUILT FOR. estate.json says this
repository runs three things and the workspaces build three BINARIES, and
they are not the same three. `focus-export` is a subcommand of the gateway
binary and not a binary at all; `tokenfuse-cluster` is a binary in the
SEPARATE crates/cluster workspace that estate.json has never heard of and
that no launcher installs.
tokenfuse-cluster is not a stub. It is a raft-replicated budget ledger, added
2026-07-02, with three integration suites (redb durability, http cluster,
kill durability) and its own CI job, `cluster (raft HA)`. The README's
architecture diagram calls it `the optional tokenfuse-cluster HA raft`.
Optional and installable-by-nothing are different things, and until this file
existed only this repository could tell them apart: a central registry cannot
see a second workspace it was never told about.
TWO WORKSPACES IS ALSO WHY THE CHECK IS WHAT IT IS. `cargo metadata` at the
root reports two binaries and stops; crates/cluster needs its own
--manifest-path. That is the same seam the two-lockfile trap sits in, which
CLAUDE.md already records for `cargo audit`, and it bites the same way here.
THE ENVIRONMENT SPLIT IS DECLARED, THE UNION IS CHECKED. There are a hundred
TOKENFUSE_ names and assigning each to the component that reads it would be
guesswork, since the gateway, the MCP surface and the cloud share a prefix
space. So the split below is organisational and by prefix, and what the test
asserts is that the UNION of the three matches every name in non-test source,
both ways. A name that moves between components does not fail; a name that
appears or disappears does.

the_component_name_is_not_the_binary_nam.why: The binary is `tokenfuse`; every launcher installs it as `tokenfuse-gateway`, which is the name estate.json and the port map use. Recorded rather than renamed: the rename would break every deployment for a tidiness nobody asked for.

the_mcp_surface_is_a_second_listener.why: The same binary serves an MCP surface on its own address from TOKENFUSE_MCP_ADDR. One component, two listeners, which this schema has no field for and which is not worth inventing one for until a second component needs it.

it_is_a_routine_not_a_binary.why: estate.json lists it beside two binaries and it is a subcommand of one of them. stack-up runs it at 06:00 against its own trace directory.

what_it_actually_is.value: a harness over a library, not a plane
what_it_actually_is.why:
CORRECTED 2026-08-28, hours after the first version of this entry called it a service nothing installs. That was true and it was the shallow half of the truth.

`crates/cluster` is a LIBRARY with a binary beside it. The gateway depends on the library behind an optional feature (`cluster = ["dep:tokenfuse-cluster"]`) and runs raft IN PROCESS, in `crates/gateway/src/raft_ledger.rs`. So HA is a MODE OF THE GATEWAY, configured by TOKENFUSE_CLUSTER_ID / _PEERS / _DATA_DIR / _BOOTSTRAP, and the standalone binary is the harness for driving that ledger by hand: an in-process three-node demo, a `demo-http` over real sockets, and a `serve` for running one node manually.

So it is a dev-tool, in the sense trailryx's seven are: nothing should install it, and its absence from every deployment is the answer rather than a question.

the_ha_capability_is_compiled_out_of_eve.why:
THIS is the finding, and it is bigger than a binary nobody installs. Every image in the estate builds the gateway WITHOUT `--features cluster`: stack-k8s's images/tokenfuse.Dockerfile, stack-single through the same file, stack-up and taipan from source. So the raft ledger is not merely unconfigured, it is absent from the binary, and the four TOKENFUSE_CLUSTER_ variables name a code path that ships nowhere.

Measured 2026-08-28 rather than argued: built with the feature, started with TOKENFUSE_CLUSTER_ID=1, BOOTSTRAP=1 and a data dir. It logged `raft storage: durable (redb)`, openraft initialised, `node-1.redb` appeared on disk and /healthz answered 200. The capability is real and one flag away.

Whether HA should ship by default is a product decision and is not made here: the feature pulls the whole openraft stack into an image every deployment runs. stack-k8s carries the recipe for turning it on deliberately.
